statement: A requestable topic becomes a tool by carrying a `tool` field. `description` and `readOnly` are required; `title`, `consequential` and `untrustedContent` are optional, and the two flags default to `false`.

events.why: Requiring `readOnly` makes every author decide whether the tool changes anything.

statement: A `tool` on a topic without `reply` is a type error, and the kernel's start check rejects it at run time.

events.why: A tool has to answer, and only a requestable topic can.

statement: Transports map the flags: `readOnly` to `readOnlyHint`, `consequential` to `consequentialHint` in WebMCP and `destructiveHint` in MCP, and `untrustedContent` to `untrustedContentHint` in WebMCP. MCP has no such hint, so the dev MCP adds a sentence to the description instead.

events.why: Agents read the hints to decide what to ask the user first; MCP's `openWorldHint` means something else.
The dev MCP's tools, M4a task 8.

statement: A tool's name is its topic's name, so a new topic version is a new tool.

events.why: Topic names already fit both WebMCP's and MCP's naming rules.

statement: A tool's input schema is its topic schema's input and its output schema is `reply`'s output, both JSON Schema draft 2020-12 made through `~standard.jsonSchema`. The host makes them once, at start.

events.why: The contract is already the source of truth for the topic's shape.

statement: `tool` and the topic's Standard Schema stay on the host. The bus never sees them, so a differing `tool` doesn't break delivery or trip the contracts-mismatch check.

events.why: The bus never acts on a tool, and transports only run on the host.
Building it put the Standard Schema on the host's `TopicShape`, so the host can make JSON Schema itself.
events.prev: `tool` stays on the host. The bus never sees it, so a differing `tool` doesn't break delivery or trip the contracts-mismatch check.

statement: Only the app's `agents.expose` patterns (grant matchers) expose tools. A `tool` field alone exposes nothing, and isolates can't expose anything themselves.

events.why: A contract shared between apps, or from another team, must not expose tools in an app that never chose to.

statement: `kernel.tools()` lists the exposed tools: name, title, description, flags, both JSON Schemas, the `timeoutMs` to pass on and the `TopicRef` to call. Every transport reads it.

events.why: One list means no transport builds schemas of its own.
A transport can't read the kernel's config or look topics up by name, so each entry carries both.
events.prev: `kernel.tools()` lists name, title, description, the flags and the two JSON Schemas.

statement: `createKernel` throws `KernelError('not_exposable')`, naming the topic, when an `expose` pattern matches a topic with no `reply`, no `tool`, a schema without `~standard.jsonSchema`, or an `unchecked` schema.

events.why: An agent needs a real input schema, so this is stricter than `isoloop contracts export`.

statement: An `expose` pattern that matches no topic is reported once through the `agents:unmatched` kernel event.

events.why: A typo in a pattern would otherwise expose nothing in silence; devtools can show the event.

statement: `kernel.request(topic, value, { key?, timeoutMs?, signal?, via? })` sends a request from the host on any requestable topic, exposed or not.

events.why: Transports would otherwise be special clients, and apps want the call for their own use.

statement: `kernel.request` rejects with a `BusError`: `not_requestable`, `invalid`, `reply_invalid`, `timeout` and `bus_unavailable` as `bus.request` does, plus `aborted` when its `signal` aborts, `no_responder` and `dropped`.

events.why: One error shape for callers, not the platform's `AbortError`.
A request retention removes before any subscriber gets it now fails at once.

statement: `kernel.request`'s `timeoutMs` defaults to the bus's request timeout.
Agent calls time out after `agents.timeoutMs`. Transports pass it from `kernel.tools()`.

events.why: Long enough for a restart and catch-up, short enough not to look broken.

statement: A host request record carries `req: { from: 'host', id, via? }`. `via` is one of `'mcp'`, `'webmcp'` or `'builder'`, and any other value rejects with `invalid`. It's a self-declared label for logging and policy, never for authorisation.

events.why: Handlers can tell agent calls apart; a closed list stops a typo slipping through.

statement: A request waits in its topic's log, so an isolate that restarts within the timeout gets the call when it resubscribes, and replies.

events.why: A crashed responder answers after its restart instead of failing the call.

statement: When retention removes a request record before the bus delivered it to any subscriber, the bus answers that caller at once with `BusError('dropped')`. It applies to an isolate's `bus.request` too.

events.why: Each such caller waited out its whole timeout; #288 measured 100 of 1,000 burst calls answered on a topic keeping 100 records.

statement: Before sending a `kernel.request`, the host checks that at least one isolate could answer: its grants allow subscribing and it isn't `stopped` or `failed`. With none, the call fails at once with `no_responder`. An isolate's own `bus.request` gets no such check.

events.why: Ten seconds of silence when every responder has given up looks like a hang, and the host already knows.

statement: A tool handler must check `req.id` before doing its work, because a crash between its side effect and its reply delivers the record again.

events.why: Delivery is at least once; for a `consequential` tool a repeat means doing the work twice.

statement: `connectDevMCP(kernel, { url, token })` from `@isoloop/host/dev-mcp` dials the `isoloop mcp` CLI's WebSocket and sends requests with `via: 'mcp'`.

events.why: A transport of its own entry, imported behind `import.meta.env.DEV`, stays out of production bundles.

statement: The `isoloop mcp` CLI accepts a page only with its token, printed on stderr each run or fixed through `ISOLOOP_MCP_TOKEN`, and only from an `Origin` matching `--origin`.

events.why: Any site open in the browser can try `ws://127.0.0.1`; without the token it gets nothing.
The dev MCP server, M4a task 6.

statement: `@isoloop/vite` fails a production build that still contains the dev MCP entry, unless the plugin is given `allowDevMcp: true`.

events.why: The dev MCP's WebSocket client must never ship by accident.

statement: Through the dev MCP, an app tool without `readOnly: true` needs the CLI's `--allow-write`.

events.why: Writes from a coding agent are opt-in for each run.
The dev MCP's reads and writes, M4a task 8.

statement: `connectWebMCP(kernel)` from `@isoloop/webmcp` registers each exposed tool with the page's WebMCP. Its `execute` calls `kernel.request` with the tool's `timeoutMs` and `via: 'webmcp'`, and a failed call rejects with the `BusError`. Without WebMCP it does nothing.

events.why: A package of its own keeps a moving draft API out of `@isoloop/host`.

statement: `connectWebMCP` uses `document.modelContext`, or `navigator.modelContext` where only that exists, never both.

events.why: Chromium puts it on `document`, Firefox on `navigator`; the code follows the features, not the browser's name.

statement: `connectWebMCP` sends each hint only when it's `true`.

events.why: Firefox reads `readOnlyHint` as true whenever it's present, which would list a consequential tool as read-only.

statement: If a tool name from `kernel.tools()` is already registered by `connectWebMCP` on the same `ModelContext`, it throws `KernelError('invalid_config')` and registers nothing.

events.why: Chromium rejects a duplicate and Firefox replaces it; refusing it ourselves behaves the same in both.

statement: `toolcancel` aborts that tool's calls in flight where `ModelContext` has `addEventListener`. Where a call gets no signal and there's no `toolcancel`, the agent can't cancel it and it runs to its reply or timeout. Disconnecting aborts every registration and call.

events.why: The draft gives each call a signal and a `toolcancel` event.
Firefox's `ModelContext` isn't an `EventTarget` and passes no signal.
events.prev: `toolcancel` aborts that call's signal, and the returned function aborts every registration.

statement: Tools stay registered with WebMCP while their isolates restart.

events.why: Agents cache tool lists; `no_responder` reports an isolate that can't answer when a call is made.

statement: There's no per-isolate grant to expose tools.

events.why: Why not let each isolate expose its own tools? A request reaches every subscriber, so the grant would gate one isolate while another answers the same call.

statement: Tools aren't a separate API beside topics, such as `kernel.registerTool(name, handler)`.

events.why: Why not a plain tool API? It would duplicate request and reply, their schemas, timeouts and restarts, and a host-side handler would run agent calls on the main thread.

statement: `via` isn't enforced; any main-thread code can set it.

events.why: Why not let only transports set `via`? On one page that needs a token scheme, and the page is one trust domain anyway.

statement: The dev MCP isn't a kernel option.

events.why: Why not `createKernel({ dev: { mcp } })`? The WebSocket client would ship in every production bundle, and the kernel can't tell a dev build from a production one.

statement: The `isoloop mcp` CLI doesn't use the official MCP SDK; it has its own server.

events.why: Why not use `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`? The surface needed is about 300 lines; the SDK's client stays a dev dependency for conformance tests.

statement: Isoloop ships no WebMCP polyfill or shim.

events.why: Why not a polyfill for browsers without WebMCP? It only helps if some agent reads it, and the dev MCP covers development; deferred to M7.
